description: We're student developers from Lucknow taking on "Dancing with the SARs" using NASA NISAR radar data to track changes on Earth's surface. We build apps with Flutter, React/Next.js and AI. Looking for teammates with Python/GIS, data analysis, machine learning, UI design or storytelling. Beginners who learn fast are welcome!
summary:
EarthPulse is an interactive Earth intelligence platform designed to make environmental monitoring easier to understand through satellite imagery and data visualization. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Dancing with the SARs,” the platform brings flood monitoring, wetland monitoring, interactive maps, and environmental analytics together in one dashboard.

EarthPulse integrates NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) flood imagery layer to help users explore flood-related observations geographically. It also provides regional monitoring views, risk indicators, and visual analytics to support awareness of changing environmental conditions.

The platform aims to make Earth observation information more accessible and understandable for students, researchers, and communities. Our goal is to turn complex environmental information into clear visual insights that can support better awareness and informed decision-making.
details:
What EarthPulse Does

EarthPulse is a web-based environmental monitoring dashboard that brings flood-related satellite imagery, wetland monitoring, interactive maps, and visual analytics into one platform.

The platform includes five main sections:

  • Overview: A central dashboard presenting environmental monitoring indicators.
  • Live Map: An interactive map that helps users explore monitored locations.
  • Flood Monitoring: A dedicated workspace for exploring flood-related information and regional risk indicators.
  • Wetland Monitoring: A section designed to support awareness of wetland environments and their changes.
  • Analytics: Visual charts and comparisons that make environmental information easier to interpret.

NASA Resource Integration

EarthPulse integrates NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) through a Web Map Service (WMS) layer to display the MODIS Combined Flood 2-Day imagery on the interactive map. Users can toggle this imagery layer to explore NASA flood observations.

The current implementation uses NASA MODIS flood imagery as a visualization layer. It does not perform independent Sentinel-1 SAR processing or generate verified real-time flood predictions. Regional risk indicators and sample dashboard metrics are illustrative demonstration data.

Technology Used

  • React.js and JavaScript for the frontend
  • Vite for development and building
  • Leaflet and React Leaflet for interactive maps
  • OpenStreetMap for map tiles
  • Recharts for charts and analytics
  • Lucide React for interface icons
  • NASA GIBS WMS for satellite flood imagery
  • Vercel for public deployment
  • GitHub for source-code hosting and version control

Benefits and Intended Impact

EarthPulse aims to make satellite-based environmental information easier to explore and understand. It provides a single interface for visualizing flood-related observations and exploring wetland monitoring concepts. It can help students, researchers, and communities better understand environmental changes and identify areas that may deserve further investigation.

Creativity and Design

The project combines satellite imagery, interactive mapping, monitoring dashboards, and visual analytics in a single interface. Its modular design makes environmental information easier to navigate and provides a foundation for future integration of SAR-based analysis and more advanced environmental datasets.

AI Assistance Disclosure

ChatGPT was used as an AI-assisted development tool for coding guidance, debugging support, and preparation of project descriptions and presentation content. The final implementation was reviewed and assembled by the project team.
